ov: The tallest, largest and heaviest living deer, known as “elk” in British English. A solitary browser of northern forests, it spends a lot of time in and around water.

why.dg: Moose aren’t usually aggressive, but when provoked or frightened they attack more people than bears and wolves combined, usually with only minor injuries.
why.et: Hunted across its range; in Sweden in 1983 moose made up 14% of all meat eaten.

rg: Northern forests of North America, northern Europe and northern Asia, from Scandinavia and the Baltic states to Russia and Mongolia.
df: Mainly a browser of branches, twigs and leaves, plus aquatic plants in summer.

cf.tip: In North America “elk” means a different species of deer. In British English “elk” means the moose.

fx: Moose have been known to dive over 5.5 m to reach plants on lake bottoms.
